en.headline: Former Democratic Party chairman Wu Chi-wai granted six-month UK stay
en.dek: British immigration authorities approved visitor status for the former legislator after an initial seven-day restriction following his arrival to visit family.
body: Former Democratic Party chairman Wu Chi-wai has been granted permission to remain in the United Kingdom for six months as a visitor, his lawyer confirmed on Monday.

Wu, who completed a prison sentence in Hong Kong last month, arrived in London to visit his family. British border officers initially restricted him to a seven-day immigration bail and retained his passport, citing concerns he might intend a longer stay. After further review, the restriction was lifted and visitor status for six months was approved, matching the usual arrangement for holders of British National (Overseas) passports.

Lawyer Paul Harris said the decision was confirmed by UK immigration authorities. Wu later released a video message thanking those who had expressed concern and stating he hoped to spend time quietly with his family. The UK Home Office declined to comment on individual cases.

zh.headline: 前民主黨主席胡志偉獲准以旅客身份留英六個月
zh.dek: 英國入境當局在重新審視後批准胡志偉以旅客身份逗留六個月，較早前的七天限制獲解除。
body: 前民主黨主席胡志偉星期一獲英國入境當局批准，以旅客身份在英國逗留六個月，其代表律師已予確認。
胡志偉上月在香港完成刑期後前往倫敦探望家人。英國邊境人員最初以他可能有意長期留英為由，只批准七天入境保釋並扣起護照。經進一步審視後，限制獲解除，並批准與一般英國國民（海外）護照持有人相同的六個月旅客身份。
律師夏博義表示，英國入境部門已通知有關決定。胡志偉其後拍片感謝各方關心，並表示希望與家人平靜相聚。英國內政部表示不會評論個別個案。
